hooks.command: [ -n "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-}" ] || exit 0; find "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" \( -name node_modules -o -name .git \) -prune -o -type d -path '*/.claude/.cc-writes' ! -path "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/.cc-writes" -empty -print 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r dir; do rmdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null && rmdir "${dir%/.cc-writes}" 2>/dev/null; done; exit 0

[ -n "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-}" ] || exit 0; remover="$HOME/.local/bin/remove-worktree"; [ -x "$remover" ] || exit 0; cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 && "$remover" --landed >/dev/null 2>&1; exit 0

allow: A subagent working inside its own git worktree (a path under <repo>/.claude/worktrees/agent-*) may create, edit, move and delete files there and run the project's install and gates: the worktree is disposable, the subagent does not commit, and the orchestrator reviews the diff before anything reaches a shared branch

The orchestrating session may land a builder worktree under <repo>/.claude/worktrees/agent-* with the orchestrate skill's `scripts/land-worktree <path>` (copies its uncommitted changes into the main checkout and stages them), commit them on the working branch, and then run `remove-worktree <path>` on that worktree (or `remove-worktree --landed` for every landed one): it refuses any worktree whose changes no checkout of the repository has committed, so nothing is lost

Against the local dev stack only (localhost URLs, or a database on localhost): creating, reading and deleting individual records whose name or email starts with qa-, and creating or signing in as the project standing QA account (qa-agent@<repo>.example), is routine verification. It never covers bulk deletes, TRUNCATE or DROP, records of real users, or any non-local host such as a staging or production domain
